meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a pleasant piece.

examples.text: Tranquilo y agradable, gracias, aunque esta maleta pesa mucho hoy.
examples.trans: Quiet and pleasant, thank you, though this suitcase weighs a lot today.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Architectural stone archway or violin bow.

examples.trans: The arch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los arcos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the archs from the door.

meanings.note: Takes indicative for known facts and subjunctive for hypotheticals.

examples.trans: We are going out even though it is raining a bit.

examples.text: Esperaré aquí aunque tarde diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will wait here even if he takes ten minutes.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Agrees with the person welcomed (bienvenido, bienvenida, bienvenidos, bienvenidas).

examples.trans: It is a welcome piece.

examples.text: Déjemelo a mí. Vamos abajo a darle la bienvenida.
examples.trans: Leave it to me. Let us go down and welcome him.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.trans: There are four tables inside.
I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Por encima = on top / over the surface.

examples.trans: Put powdered sugar on top.

examples.text: Hay un cartel encima de la puerta.
examples.trans: There is a sign above the door.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Warm everyday enthusiasm in Spain.

examples.trans: It is a great piece.

examples.text: Estupendo. ¿La ventana da a la calle o al patio?
examples.trans: Wonderful. Does the window face the street or the courtyard?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.trans: It is a favourite piece.

examples.text: ¡Solo vestidos, partituras y mi taza favorita!
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite cup!

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Older speakers in Spain warmly call a young woman hija ('my dear').

examples.trans: The daughter is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hijas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the daughters from the door.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.
What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Madre mía! is a mild, warm everyday exclamation across Spain.

examples.trans: The mother is here.

examples.text: Vemos las madres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mothers from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Stressed possessive (el mío, la mía, los míos, las mías); ¡Madre mía! = Goodness me!

examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

examples.text: Un amigo mío vive en esta calle.
examples.trans: A friend of mine lives on this street.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.
Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Nombre y apellidos = full name.

examples.trans: The name is here.

examples.text: Vemos los nombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the names from the door.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Printed music sheets for piano or voice.

examples.trans: The sheet music is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partituras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sheet music from the door.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Con permiso is said politely when stepping past someone or entering.

examples.text: El permiso es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The permission is very important here.
We talk about the permission.

pesar.gloss: to weigh (pesar mucho = to be very heavy)

meanings.en: to weigh (pesar mucho = to be very heavy)
meanings.note: Spanish says pesa mucho ('it weighs a lot') for 'it is heavy'.

examples.text: Esta caja de madera pesa bastante.
examples.trans: This wooden box is fairly heavy.

examples.text: El paquete pequeño apenas pesaba nada.
examples.trans: The small parcel weighed almost nothing.

meanings.note: De piedra = made of stone.

examples.trans: The stone is here.

examples.text: Vemos las piedras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stones from the door.

meanings.note: Planta baja = ground floor; primera planta = first floor; also a green plant.

examples.trans: The floor / storey is here.

examples.text: Vemos las plantas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the floor / storeys from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Tener una reserva = to have a booking.

examples.trans: The reservation is here.

examples.text: Vemos las reservas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the reservations from the door.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

tal.gloss: such (¿qué tal? = how is / how are?)

meanings.en: such (¿qué tal? = how is / how are?)
meanings.note: ¿Qué tal todo? is everyday Spanish for 'How is everything?'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was the trip?

examples.text: ¿Qué tal se ve la mesa aquí?
examples.trans: How does the table look here?

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los vestidos.

examples.trans: The dress is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vestidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the dresss from the door.

meanings.note: Guía de viajes = travel guide.

examples.trans: The trip is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viajes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trips from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.
